newsitem.title: GEORGIA: Georgia calls poll coinciding with Abkhaz vote.
newsitem.headline: Georgia calls poll coinciding with Abkhaz vote.

text.p: Georgian President Eduard Shevardnadze has called for a referendum among refugees from the breakaway region of Abkhazia on the same day separatists there are staging a parliamentary poll.
Shevardnadze signed a decree late on Thursday authorising the plebiscite intendeed to dilute the effect of a November 23 vote by the independence-minded Abkhaz government.
The U.N. Security Council has called for the cancellation of the vote, saying tens of thousands of Georgian refugees must return to the region before elections.

Refugees will be asked a question phrased to attract the answer "no" -- whether they support the holding of the vote before Georgia's territorial integrity is restored and displaced persons return to Abkhazia.

Abkhazia, once the subtropical beach playground of the Soviet Communist elite, has run itself as an independent state since 1993. Then, irregulars, backed by arms and ethnic brethren volunteers from Russia, drove out government troops after a year of war which killed 10,000 people.
The conflict began when Georgia sent in soldiers to put down a decision by the local parliament for more autonomy.
Ethnic Georgians used to make up around 45 percent of the region's population but most fled the war, fearing ethnic cleansing.
International organisations say that between 150,000 and 200,000 Georgian refugees want to return, except for those barred from going home for taking part in the hostilities.
Observers say Shevardnadze, who has called the vote a "pure farce", wants to kill any claim to legitimacy Abkhazia's vote might give the government of "president" Vladislav Ardzinba.
Ardzinba says the election, in which 78 mostly ethnic Abkhaz candidates are contesting 35 seats, is needed beacause the old parliament's powers have expired.
He also denies the assertions by UN and Georgian officials that most of Abkhazia's population has left the region.

"The overwhelming majority of the population is located in Abkhazia. Most of the refugees who want to return already have," he told Reuters in an interview this week, saying the UN resolution was "based on nothing".

Peace talks between Abkhazia and Georgia appear to have reached a dead end, with Tbilisi insisting Abkhazia rejoin its federal structure and the Abkhaz saying they will only agree to form a "confederative union" with the central government.
The Commonwealth of Independent States, led by Russia, has imposed a partial blockade against Abkhazia in retaliation for what it calls its "intransigence" in peace talks.
